findings.correction_outcome: Make the dependency executable without changing accepted behavior: establish the required registry admission behavior through its own behavioral RED/GREEN before T031/T032, or explicitly split minimal admission and later borrow/disposition behavior into ordered RED/GREEN slices with corresponding file ownership. findings.evidence: The accepted binding constructor requires a PreparedWorkspaceUseRegistry, and ID-S08 keeps admission Closed until exact authority, host ownership, metadata protection and the process-lifetime mutex permit Open. T031 requires behavioral Bound, denial and restart-Unknown results through that binding source; T032 promises its GREEN while listing binding, store and Web production work. T033/T034 occur later and own the registry RED/GREEN, issuer registration and closure behavior needed for the accepted admission and lifetime. Implementing those behaviors during T032 would precede their assigned RED; a declaration-only registry could compile but cannot establish the required Bound and Unknown behavior.

raw_result.summary: Complete-definition REVISE for one newly introduced tasks-owned ordering defect. All seven hashes match the pinned boundary. The SpecKit prerequisite selected this feature, and deterministic plan/task design validation returned zero errors: all 36 required implementation design IDs appear on task checklist lines. Read-only semantic analysis found coverage for FR-001–FR-012 and buildable SC-001–SC-007, while identifying the T031–T034 dependency that the deterministic check cannot detect. The 17 completed task markers and earlier IDs are preserved. Ordered prior raw plan reviews 01–15 and definition reviews 01–12 were compared; their prior PATH, launch-order, cleanup, ownership, Web, concrete-store RED and completed-status findings remain resolved. T022/T023 keep real JDT launch closed pending first-PATH and restricted-profile qualification; T035/T036 do not treat fixture evidence, a named mutex, empty restarted registry or parent PID exit as native settlement. Story 18.3 retains native borrower and reader ownership. This verdict grants no implementation approval, resource permission or native readiness.
